articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Wind Turbine Monitoring System Based on Wireless Sensor Network
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Electronics and Electrical Engineering Technology (EEET)
abstract: This article studies the wind turbine monitoring system based on wireless sensor network (WSN) and proposes a low-power, low-cost, and highly flexible wireless ad hoc network technology solution. The LEACH layered routing protocol is used to improve network energy efficiency. LEACH reduces communication overhead and extends node lifespan by dynamically selecting cluster heads and aggregating data. The study provides a detailed introduction to the cluster head election mechanism and data transmission process of LEACH, and discusses its advantages in energy balance, data aggregation, distributed control, and other aspects. Based on the characteristics of the XN297L communication module, the system has achieved real-time monitoring of wind turbines, and the effectiveness and application prospects of this scheme have been experimentally verified.

articleTitle: A Study of Electric Load Forecasting Technique Using LSTM Model
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Electronics and Electrical Engineering Technology (EEET)
abstract: Electric load forecasting is crucial for efficiently operating and planning electrical power systems. Accurate load forecasts can lead to improved resource management, reduced operational costs, and enhanced reliability of power supply. This study discusses forecasting techniques. Finally, employ a Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) model, a type of Recurrent Neural Network (RNN), to predict electrical load based on historical load data and additional factors such as temperature, humidity, and public holidays. The results demonstrate the effectiveness of LSTM in capturing the temporal dependencies and trends in load data, leading to high forecasting accuracy. The LSTM model achieves a Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) of less than 10%, indicating its robustness and reliability in predicting electrical load.

articleTitle: Reflective acoustic metasurface design by moving morphable components and genetic algorithms
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Electronics and Electrical Engineering Technology (EEET)
abstract: We design reflective acoustic metasurfaces using moving morphable components and genetic algorithms. The presented method is applied to local and nonlocal design of acoustic devices. In the local design approach, individual unit cells are optimized independently based on the generalized Snell’s law (GSL) to manipulate wavefronts through phase gradient along the surface. In contrast, the nonlocal approach optimizes a supercell based on the diffraction theory, allowing consideration of interactions between unit cells. Significant performance improvement of the metasurface is observed, particularly for the larger reflection angle, where the local approach using GSL encounters limitations. This work demonstrates the potential of the presented method in advancing the design of acoustic metasurfaces.

articleTitle: Silicon based SPAD active quenching reset integrated circuit based on CMOS technology
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Electronics and Electrical Engineering Technology (EEET)
abstract: Single photon detection technology has an important research prospect in the field of optical communication. In this paper, an active quench reset circuit is designed and built for the working state of single photon avalanche diode in Geiger mode, which realizes the detection of weak near infrared light signal. Several peripheral circuits are used to detect and amplify the current of SPAD avalanche, which improves the rate of single photon detection and reduces the dead time of SPAD. The quenching reset time is 115ns, and the counting frequency is 8.7MHz.

articleTitle: Enhancing Inverter Reliability and Efficiency through Demand Control for Temperature Reduction: A Review of Literature
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Electronics and Electrical Engineering Technology (EEET)
abstract: The semiconductor components that the inverter is mostly composed of are delicate and easily damaged by variations in environmental and operational conditions. Due to these environmental and conditional variations, the temperature in the inverter increases, causing thermal stress that can lead to the failure of inverters. It has been found that this change in junction temperature is the key challenge and root cause of fatigue, aging, and finally the failure of the inverters. This paper presents a short review of the existing techniques and algorithms that are modeled to reduce the junction temperature to enhance the performance and lifetime of the inverter. Research in the literature addresses the junction temperature challenges by methods that control power flow, voltage regulation, estimate junction temperature, and evaluate the reliability of the inverter. This paper also recommends possible future research to enhance inverter reliability and performance.

articleTitle: Predicting the State of Energy Utilisation Based on Hidden Markov Model (HMM)
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Electronics and Electrical Engineering Technology (EEET)
abstract: This paper presents the utilisation of the hidden Markov model (HMM) to predict the state of energy utilisation of light. A dataset of light energy utilisation is used to develop an HMM model with two (2) components/states. The trained model is tested on a separate set of data to investigate the performance of the developed model. The results showed that the model can predict the state of energy utilisation of the lights in a house. This prediction can be used to detect the occupation in a room which can be useful for demand side management.

articleTitle: A Low-Power Low-Cost CML-Based Divider-by-2 with Quadrature Outputs
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Electronics and Electrical Engineering Technology (EEET)
abstract: An RF divider-by-2 with quadrature outputs was designed in 65-nm CMOS technology. The divider consists of two cascaded current-mode logic (CML) latches that are cross- coupled, achieving a frequency range of 2 ~ 9.5 GHz with the sensitivity from −38.9 dBm to 0 dBm. The proposed divider consumes 0.47 mW from a 1.2-V supply and has a core area of 528 µm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>. The phase noise of −138.9 dBc/Hz at 1-MHz offset frequency is also accomplished. With tri-state inverter based cross-couple structure, the presented circuit contributes to a low- power low-cost design of RF quadrature signal generators with the phase error less than 1.6°.

articleTitle: Interleaved Triangular Current Mode Totem-Pole PFC Light Load Frequency Limiting Strategy
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Electronics and Electrical Engineering Technology (EEET)
abstract: This paper proposes a light-load frequency limiting method for interleaved triangular current mode (TCM)-controlled bridgeless totem-pole power factor correction (PFC). With the development of third-generation wide bandgap semiconductors, bridgeless totem-pole PFC converters have been widely used in the field of front-end PFC converters due to their advantages of fewer components and a wide zero-voltage switching (ZVS) range. The TCM control method has been used in converters to achieve full-range ZVS. However, when the PFC converter operates under light load, the switching frequency is extremely high, resulting in significant switching losses. Additionally, the TCM control method results in larger current ripple, increasing the current stress on power devices and the core size. By deriving the current control formula under the set maximum frequency limit and introducing interleaved parallel control, the issues of high switching frequency under light load and large current ripple under TCM control are resolved. Measurement results are provided to validate the concept and design process.

articleTitle: Modelling the Impact of Uncoordinated Plug-In Electric Vehicles’ Charging Patterns on the Low Voltage Distribution Network
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Electronics and Electrical Engineering Technology (EEET)
abstract: South Africa’s existing infrastructure predates the widespread adoption of PEVs, given the current energy crisis, the introduction of Plug-in electric vehicles (PEVs) charging activities into residential Low Voltage Distribution Network (LVDN) is anticipated to have adverse impact on various LVDN system parameters, such as potential for overloading transformers and lines, as well as the possibility of exceeding the voltage’s safe operational limits. This study models the impact of PEV charging activities on South Africa’s LVDN. Key factors to the study are, Voltage Unbalance Factor (VUF) and the Voltage Profile. Three scenarios are presented as case studies: Where Case Study 1 and 2 assesses PEV charging activities on the most and least loaded phase of the provided unbalanced network, including upstream and downstream charging at 50% and 100% charging rates, respectively. Results, show that integration on heavily loaded phases could potentially destabilize the network while charging on a least loaded phase reduces the unbalance factor. Case Study 3 adopts a stochastic approach to integrate PEVs into the network, providing a more realistic and dynamic overview of the potential impact. The LVDN and load profiles utilized in this study are derived from real-life data obtained from the City of Cape Town.

articleTitle: 3D Facial Landmark Detection Techniques: A Survey
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Electronics and Electrical Engineering Technology (EEET)
abstract: In this paper, the 3D facial landmark detection methods in recent years are reviewed. Specifically, the article details 2D and 3D facial landmark detection technologies. In addition, the paper also discusses the application practice of 3D facial landmark detection and the dataset required for related research. Through this research, this paper aims to provide a reference for relevant researchers to understand the problem of 3D facial landmark detection and related research directions, so as to further study and explore this field.

articleTitle: Modular Anti-noise Deep Learning Network for Robotic Grasp Detection Based on RGB Images
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Electronics and Electrical Engineering Technology (EEET)
abstract: While traditional methods rely on depth sensors, the current trend leans towards utilizing cost-effective RGB images, despite their absence of depth cues. This paper introduces an interesting approach to detecting grasping poses from a single RGB image. To this end, we propose a modular learning network augmented with grasp detection and semantic segmentation, tailored for robots equipped with parallel-plate grippers. Our network not only identifies graspable objects but also fuses prior grasp analyses with semantic segmentation, thereby boosting grasp detection precision. Significantly, our design exhibits resilience, adeptly handling blurred and noisy visuals. Key contributions encompass a trainable network for grasp detection from RGB images, a modular design facilitating feasible grasp implementation, and an architecture robust against common image distortions. We demonstrate the feasibility and accuracy of our proposed approach through practical experiments and evaluations.

articleTitle: Wireless Sensor Network intrusion detection based on Borderline-SMOTE and Deep Ensemble Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Electronics and Electrical Engineering Technology (EEET)
abstract: With the development of the Internet of Things (IoT), Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) are widely used in several fields. Due to limited node resources and vulnerability to attacks, AI-driven intrusion detection systems have become the main means. However, the imbalance of data categories and the diversity of attack types lead to limited detection performance, so for the problems of scarce attack samples in the dataset and insufficient performance and generalization ability of traditional models, this paper proposes a WSN intrusion detection method that combines Borderline-SMOTE oversampling and deep ensemble learning. The method effectively balances the sample distribution and ensemble LSTM, CNN and ANN models to significantly improve the detection accuracy and robustness. Experimental results show that based on the WSN-DS dataset, the method achieves an accuracy of 99.20% in detecting multiple attack types, which is better than the traditional methods, especially in the F1 scores for Blackhole, Grayhole, and Flooding attacks, providing an effective solution for WSN security.

articleTitle: Advancing AI Safely: Frameworks and Strategies for the Development of GPT-5 and Beyond
publicationTitle: 2024 7th International Conference on Electronics and Electrical Engineering Technology (EEET)
abstract: The ongoing development of advanced language models like GPT-5 presents significant opportunities and challenges. This paper advocates for the continued progress of such models, emphasizing that concerns about AI safety should not halt development. This paper proposes a comprehensive framework for Universal Approximators and a robust testing mechanism to evaluate the safety of large language models (LLMs). This includes tools and a collaborative research repository. Mathematical models are presented to demonstrate that LLMs can be trained to align with specific value systems, ensuring they prioritize humanity’s well-being over potential risks such as adversarial threats. I argue that the social benefits of AI, such as solving major global challenges, outweigh the associated risks. Stronger, more intelligent models should be developed by governments and large corporations that have the resources to maintain safety and balance. Addressing concerns about job loss and cultural bias, I highlight the need for continued research and adaptation to harness AI’s potential while mitigating harm. With careful planning and alignment, AI can enhance our lives and address significant issues facing humanity.
